markers.title: The advertised assistant and the real one are two different products
markers.finding: Candidates met a terms gate and a disabled composer before the first question, in a widget that did not look like the brand that advertised it.
markers.decision: Build the one the brand promised: black bubbles, red answers, and the first thing on screen is the first question.
markers.rejected: Restyling the vendor widget, which still opens on a terms dialog.

markers.title: Five, because five is what changes a decision
markers.finding: The old application was a multi-system form that asked more than it decided, and managers then re-keyed the answers into another system anyway.
markers.decision: Minimum age, work rights, availability, shifts a week, and the high-demand shift. Nothing else is asked, because nothing else changes what happens next.
markers.rejected: A shorter version of the same form. The delay was in the routing after the form, not only in the form.

markers.title: Answers are tapped, not typed
markers.finding: First-job candidates abandoned fields that rejected their input without saying why, and a date of birth field is the worst of them.
markers.decision: Every answer is a chip. There is no format to get wrong, and the whole set is visible, so a candidate can see what they are choosing between.
markers.rejected: Free text with validation, which is a quiz where the rules are only revealed when you fail.

markers.title: Every question says why it is asked
markers.finding: Candidates read a screening question about availability as a test they could fail, and answered what they thought was wanted rather than what was true.
markers.decision: One line under each question saying what it decides. An honest answer is more useful than a flattering one, and saying so is what gets it.
markers.rejected: Explaining nothing, which is how a form full of reasonable questions reads as an interrogation.

markers.title: The hard question is asked last
markers.finding: The high-demand shift is the one the restaurant is genuinely short of, and leading with it reads as the only thing that matters.
markers.decision: It is question five. By then the candidate knows what the job is, and a no on this question is a conversation rather than an exit.
markers.rejected: Asking it first as a qualifier, which turns the most valuable applicants away before they know what they are turning down.
